topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and sets out the core learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address conventional cancer treatment modalities, including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutics, along with their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic molecular defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependency, checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair pathways through synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver kinases, analyzing their mechanisms of action alongside the mutation, bypass, and addiction pathways that cause resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how monoclonal antibodies are used directly to inhibit receptor signaling or engineered as conjugates to deliver cytotoxic agents selectively to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and cell-based immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the principles of antitumor immunity and modern immunotherapeutic approaches, encompassing immune checkpoint blockade, neoantigen recognition, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Clinical progress, challenges, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize historical trends in cancer mortality, ongoing therapeutic challenges, future research directions, and the ethical dilemmas of clinical trials.
